channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Environmental agency confirms burning of economic trees threatens food security and exacerbates climate change effects.

item.title: African youth protest deepening political dissatisfaction
item.description: Protests erupted in Kenya, Tanzania, Morocco and beyond demanding better governance amid economic hardship.

item.title: Shankerdas & Sons signs local content agreement
item.description: The company commits to increasing Sierra Leonean employment and skills development.

item.title: Tanzania mobilizes funds for 83bn/- Babati market
item.description: The new market in Manyara Region will accommodate 810 traders, replacing an overcrowded 1977 facility.

item.title: Togo government in exile demands ECOWAS court order enforcement
item.description: The legitimate government and DMK announced a forced execution order for a January 29, 2026 ECOWAS court ruling.

item.title: Moroccan film week opens in Abidjan to boost coproduction
item.description: Ivory Coast and Morocco aim to move from film screenings to joint creation and investment.

item.title: Namibia private sector credit grows N$5.84 billion in nine months
item.description: Nominal borrowing increased by 39% year-on-year, but inflation is eroding real gains, Simonis Storm reports.

item.title: Algerian parliament to review fuel price changes
item.description: A finance committee proposed that parliament must approve any fuel price adjustments for 2027.

item.title: Togo mayor deploys beauty brigade to clear sidewalks
item.description: Golfe 5 commune launches a two-week operation to remove goods and structures from priority streets.

item.title: Two arrested for election offences in Limpopo
item.description: Suspects detained for tearing down posters and assault ahead of local government elections.

item.title: Tanzania plans cold rooms to cut crop waste
item.description: The government is exploring simple technology to preserve perishable produce like bananas and vegetables.

item.title: Namibia diesel price passes N$30 per litre
item.description: Petrol also rises as higher shipping costs and a weaker currency increase fuel import expenses.

item.title: Victoria Falls entertainment spot ordered to lower music volume
item.description: A High Court ruling restricts Tshisa Nyama's music hours following a complaint from a local hospitality operator.

item.title: Chad officials urge herders to respect transhumance dates
item.description: Authorities in Loug-Chari are meeting with nomadic herders to ensure they arrive after December 15.

item.title: Egypt parliament approves fund for martyrs' families
item.description: Amendments to the law governing the Fund for Honoring Martyrs aim to remove obstacles for beneficiaries.

item.title: Cédric Diarra's age remains undisclosed
item.description: The vice-president of Ivory Coast's National Assembly, Cédric Tidiane Diarra, is 44 or 45 years old.

item.title: Tanzania eyes global energy investment at ADIPEC
item.description: The nation aims to attract capital for its 57.54 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and renewable energy projects.

item.title: Rwanda secures $4.97M for climate adaptation
item.description: The funds will support smallholder farmers in Gatsibo, Nyagatare, and Kayonza districts with climate-smart technologies.

item.title: Windhoek builds N$4.7 million market for 46 traders
item.description: The City of Windhoek is constructing a new market opposite Shoprite, with Debmarine Namibia contributing N$3.2 million towards the project.

item.title: Ghana urged not to revoke mining lease over debt
item.description: Dr Steve Manteaw advises negotiation for US$8.38 million owed by Northern Ashanti Mines.

item.title: Zimbabwe hosts Southern Africa Insurance Indaba
item.description: The four-day event in Victoria Falls will focus on futureproofing African insurance.

item.title: Police rescue 11 kidnapped victims
item.description: 19 suspects arrested and 91 livestock recovered in security operations across several states.

item.title: Rival SPLA-IO factions clash in Leer, killing five soldiers
item.description: Fighting erupted between forces loyal to Nathaniel Oyet and Regina Joseph Kaba, following Kaba's appointment as acting chairperson.

item.title: Drones strike Sudan power stations
item.description: Fires broke out at electricity facilities in Kassala State after multiple drone attacks on Monday morning.

item.title: South Sudan governor receives three tractors for farming
item.description: The equipment, donated by the Presidency, aims to boost food production and improve produce transport to markets.

item.title: Tanzania minister meets King Charles III at CHOGM
item.description: Ambassador Mahmoud Thabit Kombo discussed investment and economic growth with leaders in Antigua.

item.title: ADC says Atiku won't pick Senate President, Speaker
item.description: Dino Melaye stated the African Democratic Congress will allow lawmakers to elect their own leaders for independence.

item.title: Chad health officials review maternity network
item.description: Health leaders in Moyen-Chari, Mandoul, and Logone Oriental are meeting in Sarh to improve emergency obstetric and neonatal care.

item.title: Algerian workers warned over job burnout signs
item.description: A study found links between workplace rudeness and employees wanting to leave their jobs.

item.title: Ivory Coast intensifies animal disease surveillance
item.description: Health, animal and environmental sectors train in Grand-Bassam on zoonotic disease detection.

item.title: Mozambique government to brief parliament on health, roads, and climate
item.description: Parliamentary groups demand details on El Niño impact, National Road 1 repairs, and Nampula General Hospital construction delays.

item.title: Liberian businesswomen petition legislature over import delays
item.description: Traders cite three to six-month shipping times and high bank charges as threats to local enterprises.

item.title: Ivory Coast opens digital farming school
item.description: The Digital Farming School in Yamoussoukro will train 50 students annually in tech for agriculture.

item.title: ZIMRA sets November tax deadlines
item.description: Taxpayers must submit returns by November 5 and payments by November 10.

item.title: Zimbabwe shares HIV funding model with Tanzania
item.description: The AIDS Levy is highlighted as a key mechanism for mobilising local resources for HIV programmes.

item.title: SAHRC flags R777m tanker bill amid Gauteng water crisis
item.description: The South African Human Rights Commission found infrastructure failure, not water shortage, causes outages.

item.title: Malian women's group collects over 58 million FCFA
item.description: The Femmes solidaires et autonomes du Mali announced their 2026 financial contributions at their annual general assembly.

item.title: Liberia to register 140,000 migrants
item.description: Government launches biometric exercise for foreign nationals, primarily from Burkina Faso, due to security concerns.

item.title: N'Djamena ice factory shut for hygiene breaches
item.description: Municipal sanitary police closed an ice production unit in N'Djamena on November 2, 2026, after finding serious hygiene failures.

item.title: South Sudan Ebola preparedness exercise reveals gaps
item.description: A simulation exercise in Juba, Yei, and Yambio identified shortcomings in emergency referrals and sample handling.

item.title: Seychellois elders and youth unite for Creole Language Day
item.description: A group of elders and young Seychellois people met to share experiences and discuss during a workshop.

item.title: Maputo Central Hospital resumes cancer treatment after fire
item.description: 95 percent of patient records were saved from the blaze that damaged the oncology unit.

item.title: UN mission ends, Western Sahara risks escalation
item.description: Financial Times warns of unprecedented uncertainty and potential military confrontation after MINURSO's 35-year mandate expires.

item.title: ADM opens Nairobi office to boost East African trade
item.description: The global nutrition and agricultural company aims to connect local demand with its worldwide supply chain network.

item.title: Content creator visits 100th country
item.description: Orsolya Zombati chose Seychelles as her 100th country to visit and create videos and images.

item.title: Mauritius baby dies from intestinal tear
item.description: A one-month-old infant died after suffering a laceration to the intestine, according to an autopsy.

item.title: Tunisia president revives Djerba bridge project
item.description: President Kaïs Saïed discussed a 2.4-kilometer bridge linking Djerba to the mainland with his infrastructure minister.

item.title: Comoros radio journalist Mselem Ali dies
item.description: Mselem Ali, a prominent voice on Comorian radio, passed away after a career marked by significant media evolution and challenges.

item.title: Mozambique's former defence minister Joaquim Tobias Dai dies
item.description: Dai served as minister from 2000 to 2008 and was a veteran of the National Liberation Struggle.

item.title: Equatorial Guinean goalkeeper injures opponent
item.description: Jesús Lázaro Owono's collision with Jesús de Miguel during a Spanish Segunda División match caused immediate concern.

item.title: Two fugitives recaptured in Mauritius
item.description: Stéphane Perrine and Jeff Wendy Leonel Domingue escaped on Saturday and were found Sunday.

item.title: South Darfur trains Ebola response teams
item.description: Rapid response teams in Sudan's South Darfur State received training to detect Ebola at borders with Central African Republic and South Sudan.

item.title: Mozambique plans $189.8 million agricultural campaign
item.description: The 2026/27 plan includes emergency support for producers affected by El Niño and investment in agribusiness.

item.title: Ecama backs Malawi's tight monetary policy
item.description: The Economics Association of Malawi supports the Reserve Bank's decision to keep interest rates high due to inflation and El Niño.

item.title: US Embassy gives Bel Eau primary school playground
item.description: The American Embassy provided new playground structures for children at Bel Eau Primary School.

item.title: Former Attorney General Paul Kihara dies aged 72
item.description: The Judiciary has paid tribute to the distinguished jurist for his enduring contribution to Kenya’s legal institutions.

item.title: McGill claims CDC would have won 2023 election
item.description: Former minister Nathaniel McGill stated the ruling Unity Party would not have won the 2023 presidential elections if he had remained in government.

item.title: Dogo-bis programme recruits eight for Benin unit
item.description: The Benin Republic's Presidency seeks staff for a $150 million World Bank-funded project.

item.title: Seychelles arms import inquiry presents report
item.description: A commission heard testimony from 99 individuals and reviewed 378 documents over 10 months.

item.title: Liberia senator demands speedy trial over US$425,000 equipment deal
item.description: Gbarpolu County citizens call for Superintendent Sam K. Zinnah's recusal amid allegations of financial misconduct.

item.title: Liberia police suspend four officers for misconduct
item.description: One officer faces criminal investigation for alleged assault, corruption, and gross insubordination.

item.title: Central African Republic leader uses new constitution for life term
item.description: President Touadéra's March 30, 2026 inauguration solidifies his grip on power, resetting previous mandates.

item.title: Kenya restricts Diwali fireworks to four hours
item.description: Mining CS Joho mandates permits and limits shell size for celebrations from November 6 to 8.

item.title: Moody's upgrades Zambia's credit rating to Caa1
item.description: The rating agency cited progress in debt restructuring and fiscal consolidation following the country's 2020 default.

item.title: Mali state security holds lawyer for six months
item.description: Mountaga Tall, a former minister and democracy advocate, was abducted from his home by state security agents.

item.title: Ecobank posts $737 million profit before tax
item.description: The pan-African banking group's profit before tax rose 12% to $737 million in the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: Benin student wins international writing prize
item.description: Chekpo Marie-Ange S. D., 15, received a special mention at the 55th Universal Postal Union competition.

item.title: Man killed with machete in Ouénou
item.description: A man in his fifties died after a machete attack by his neighbor on November 1, 2026.

item.title: Libya braces for Mediterranean storm Agnetta
item.description: The storm is centered south of Italy and moving east with active winds and low pressure.

item.title: Benin ranks 12th in Africa governance index
item.description: The country scores 60.1 points, exceeding continental and West African averages despite political participation decline.

item.title: UN begins withdrawing peacekeepers from Western Sahara
item.description: The UN mission in Western Sahara is closing its 13 sites after its mandate was not extended by the Security Council.

item.title: Ghana envoy expects US police to identify teen killer
item.description: Ambassador Victor Emmanuel Smith seeks motive for the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Javits Badu Nkansah Frimpong in New York.

item.title: Tunisia forecasts warmer, drier winter
item.description: Temperatures are expected to be above seasonal norms from November 2026 to January 2027, with less rain than usual.

item.title: Malawi farmers fear hunger over fertiliser delays
item.description: Thousands of growers have not received subsidised inputs, threatening the next harvest as planting rains approach.

item.title: Illegal mining threatens Ghana's regional diplomacy
item.description: Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings warns shared rivers polluted by mining could spill toxic waters into Côte d'Ivoire.

item.title: Adfs free nearly 50 hostages in Ituri
item.description: Nearly 50 people held for weeks by ADF rebels have regained their freedom in the Malembi forest.

item.title: Bill Clinton Foundation warns of Ndolo prison overcrowding
item.description: The foundation urges Congolese authorities to take urgent action to alleviate severe overcrowding at the Ndolo military prison.

item.title: JUSAG strike grounds Cape Coast courts
item.description: Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana members began an indefinite strike on Monday, November 2, over unapproved salary reviews.

item.title: Heavy rains blow roof off zambian teacher's house
item.description: Buyaka Primary School in Kawambwa District faces infrastructure concerns ahead of El Nino.

item.title: Central African Republic ranks 50th out of 54 African nations in governance index
item.description: The country scores 31.3 out of 100, falling below the continental average and showing a decline in key areas.

item.title: Andrada mining contribution rises to N$775.2 million
item.description: The company's direct economic impact grew 6% in the 2026 financial year, driven by wages and local procurement.

item.title: Senegal parliament debates budget correction
item.description: Lawmakers are set to vote on a revised 2026 budget, with opposition lawmakers expressing concerns.

item.title: Mafia leader Haibado Ismail Omar reportedly takes charge
item.description: Haibado Ismail Omar is named as the new leader of Qawlaysato, Africa's oldest mafia organization.

item.title: Ghana's urban population reaches 19.8 million
item.description: Nearly two million young people aged 15 to 35 are neither employed nor in education or training.

item.title: Jinhua trade with Africa reaches 161.41 billion yuan
item.description: Chinese city's exports to Africa, led by new energy products, grew 29.6% in nine months.

item.title: Antananarivo traffic chaos as roadworks begin
item.description: Road construction on two key arteries will last until January 16, 2027, causing severe congestion.

item.title: Madagascar economist urges digital law for growth
item.description: Jonah Andrianantoanina says updated legislation will help Madagascar leverage AI and improve internet access.

item.title: Eswatini Competition Commission probes EswatiniMed
item.description: Medical aid fund EswatiniMed faces investigation for alleged anti-competitive practices against rival providers.

item.title: Eswatini names Malta friendly squad
item.description: Interim coach Dominic Kunene recalls midfielder Quality Dlamini for November 12 match.

item.title: Tribunal rules for ITQNET in E8.8m tax dispute
item.description: Eswatini Revenue Service failed to respond to ITQNET's objection within a reasonable period.

item.title: Morocco justice minister pledges illicit enrichment law
item.description: Abdellatif Ouahbi faces parliamentary pressure for delayed anti-corruption reforms including asset declarations and whistleblower protections.

item.title: Beyla identifies 33 tourist sites
item.description: Access difficulties and poor road conditions hinder the development of natural and historical attractions.

item.title: Malawi opposition leader attacks divisive politics
item.description: Simplex Chithyola-Banda says rewarding loyalty over competence hinders national development.

item.title: Morocco extends fuel subsidies for transport operators
item.description: Government offers financial support for passenger and freight carriers as diesel prices rise.

item.title: Morocco faces buffer zone uncertainty after MINURSO withdrawal
item.description: The Polisario Front has declared itself no longer bound by a 1997 military agreement governing the buffer zone.

item.title: Tunis hosts 11th human rights film festival
item.description: The festival runs November 3-7, 2026, at Ciné-Théâtre Le Rio with a focus on climate justice.

item.title: Burkina Faso launches digital university research project
item.description: The four-year Digit OACS project, funded by Germany, will analyze digital practices in universities across Burkina Faso, Kenya, and Nigeria.

item.title: Senegalese teacher arrested for visa scam
item.description: Police in Mbacké apprehended a Dakar school supervisor accused of defrauding clients of over 25 million CFA francs.

item.title: Mauritanian journalists host regional press meeting
item.description: Noukchott will host 21 press leaders from the Arab world and Middle East to discuss journalist challenges.

item.title: Senegal aims for 48.5% emissions cut by 2035
item.description: The nation needs $24.9 billion for its climate goals, with most expected from international partners.
